descriptionChirho: The state or condition of social shame, dishonor, or reproach borne by a person, group, or nation, encompassing all grammatical inflections, possessive suffixes, and prepositional constructions; confirmed by Arabic cognate عار (ʿār, shame/disgrace), Korean 수치/치욕 (shame/humiliation), and Swahili aibu (shame).

Active words of scorn, censure, or insult spoken against someone, emphasizing the speech-act of reviling rather than the resulting state of shame; distinguished by Arabic تَعْيِير (taʿyīr, taunting/reviling) rather than عار, Korean 비난 (censure), and Swahili matusi (insults).

An inherent fault, moral defect, or condition that itself constitutes a cause of disgrace, rather than externally imposed shame; distinguished by Arabic عَيْب (ʿayb, fault/defect/blemish) instead of عار, indicating something intrinsically disgraceful.
